title: The best San Diego beach for your trip: families, surfers, long walks and tide pools
excerpt: Which San Diego beach suits young kids, surfers, a long quiet walk or a morning of tide pools and seals, plus the city beach rules worth knowing before you pack the cooler.

seo.title: Best San Diego Beaches by Trip: Kids, Surf, Tide Pools
seo.description: Which San Diego beach fits your trip: calm water for kids, surf breaks, long walks, tide pools and seals, plus the beach rules and winter hours to know.

heroCaption: The La Jolla coastline from above, from the listing photos of one of Cardo's La Jolla homes.
bodyHtml:
San Diego's beaches are not interchangeable. Some have gentle waves and a lifeguard all year; others suit a long walk or an hour among the tide pools. Here is how to match the beach to the trip, with the rules and winter hours that catch visitors out.

As of November 2026

Hours, fees and closures come from the City of San Diego, California State Parks, the National Park Service and the County of San Diego, linked where they appear.

Which San Diego beach is best for young kids?

For most families, La Jolla Shores. The City says its summer waves are usually the gentlest of any San Diego beach, and it is one of nine city beaches with a permanent lifeguard station. Restrooms, showers, a playground and picnic areas sit right behind the sand. For water with no waves at all, try Mission Bay or the bay side of Silver Strand.

The beach borders the La Jolla Underwater Park, where fishing and taking anything from the water are prohibited (City of San Diego).

Mission Bay has no surf and no significant currents, which makes it popular with toddlers. Two cautions from the City: some beaches have a sudden drop-off, where a child who is waist deep can take one step and go under, and between November and spring break there are no lifeguards on duty anywhere in the bay. In winter, La Jolla Shores is the safer pick.

Across the bay from downtown, Silver Strand State Beach has sand on both the ocean and San Diego Bay, and State Parks describes the bay water as usually warmer and calmer. Vehicle day use runs $12 to $20 depending on demand, and in winter (November through February) the gates close at 7 p.m.

Where should surfers go?

It depends on your level and the swell. Our separate guide to where to surf in San Diego by level covers beginner breaks, the spots for stronger surfers, board rentals and lessons, lineup etiquette and the best tides.

Which beach is best for a long, quiet walk?

Torrey Pines State Beach. It runs about 4.5 miles from Del Mar south past Los Peñasquitos Lagoon to the sandstone cliffs below Torrey Pines Mesa. Go at low tide, when there is more sand between the cliffs and the waves, and stay at least 10 feet from the base of the bluffs: rockslides happen without warning.

According to California State Parks, the gates open at 7:15 a.m. and close at sunset. Parking costs $15 to $20 in the South Beach lot and $10 to $25 in the North Beach lot, both priced by demand. Dogs are not allowed anywhere on the beach or in the reserve, including inside parked cars.

Where can you see tide pools and seals?

The tide pools at Cabrillo National Monument on Point Loma, and the harbor seals at the Children's Pool in La Jolla. Late fall and winter are the best months for tide pools, because the lowest tides fall in daylight.

The National Park Service opens the tide pool area at 9 a.m. and, for most of the year, closes it at 4:30 p.m. Plan to arrive within two hours either side of low tide, ideally a tide of 0.7 feet or lower; the park publishes monthly tide tables. Taking anything, including shells and rocks, is prohibited, and an entrance fee may apply.

Harbor seals rest at the Children's Pool all year. The beach itself is closed to people from December 15 through May 15 for pupping season, but the area stays a popular spot to watch them. Give the animals their space.

What rules apply on San Diego city beaches?

Alcohol, glass containers and smoking are all banned on City of San Diego beaches, and the ban covers the cliffs, walkways, park areas and adjacent parking lots too. Fires are allowed only inside fire containers and never between midnight and 5 a.m. (City beach regulations).

Dogs are barred from city beaches from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. between November and March, and from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. the rest of the year. The off-leash options are in our guide to San Diego with a dog.

After rain, the County of San Diego advises staying out of ocean and bay water for 72 hours once the rain stops, because runoff raises bacteria levels. Check sdbeachinfo.com for current advisories and closures before you swim.

Where to stay for the beach you picked

A home within walking distance saves the parking hunt. For La Jolla Shores and the Children's Pool, look at La Jolla; for calm-water days on the bay, Mission Beach and Pacific Beach; for Silver Strand, Coronado. You can browse Cardo's homes by neighborhood and dates on our booking site.
